stories.title: More physical disability went with poorer thinking skills in MS
stories.summary: A review of 223 studies found greater physical disability was linked to lower scores on thinking tests, mostly in advanced disease. Thinking problems also showed up with mild physical disability.
stories.why: Thinking changes can be missed by standard disability checks.

stories.title: Rituximab tied to a higher chance of bowel disease in a large Swedish study
stories.summary: In nearly 14,000 treatment episodes, bowel disease (mostly Crohn's) was more common with rituximab than with three other MS drugs. It was still rare: under 2% of people in any group within 10 years. This is a link, not proof.
stories.why: If you take rituximab, this is something to ask your neurologist about; the study says the risk should be weighed against its benefits.

stories.title: Experts: MS activity, day-to-day impact and progression are separate things
stories.summary: In a panel discussion, MS specialists said inflammation, everyday symptoms and slow worsening of disability can each happen without the others. They say treatments now control relapses well, so future work should focus on progression. This is expert opinion, not a new study.

stories.title: Blood tests for MS activity are moving toward routine use, company expert says
stories.summary: In an interview, a maker of an MS blood test said such tests may catch silent disease activity and help with treatment choices. Insurance coverage and access to blood draws remain hurdles. This is company news, and its ability to predict future disease is not yet shown.

stories.title: Nasal spray foralumab: mixed results in a small progressive MS trial
stories.summary: Company news: a small phase 2 trial in non-active secondary progressive MS found the lower dose reduced a brain-inflammation marker on PET scans versus placebo, but the higher dose did not. The company has not released the full data.
stories.why: It is early and small, and no change in disability was seen, so it is not yet a proven treatment.

stories.title: Jack Osbourne says he sometimes feels like a "fraud" at MS events
stories.summary: On a podcast, he said he has met newer patients facing harder struggles than his. He added that MS has slowed him down at times but has not stopped him.
stories.why: Many people with MS feel they do not belong, or are not "sick enough", and he says so openly.

stories.title: Free online MS Q&A with experts, Thursday evening
stories.summary: Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is holding a free virtual question-and-answer session on Thursday, November 5, from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m. Topics include aging with MS, symptoms, diet, exercise, medicines and research.

stories.title: National MS Society opens funding for early-detection screening tools
stories.summary: The Society is asking researchers to apply for money to build and test MS screening tools that are practical to use. This is a funding call from the Society, not a study result.
stories.source: Targeted News Service (National MS Society release)

stories.title: Review finds little proof that a gluten-free diet helps MS
stories.summary: A review of six small studies found possible gains in fatigue and quality of life, but no convincing effect on MS activity or disability. The evidence was rated very low certainty, and many studies were not randomized.
stories.why: It is unclear whether any benefit came from avoiding gluten or from other diet changes made at the same time.

stories.title: Canada approves Ocrevus for children with relapsing MS
stories.summary: Health Canada approved Ocrevus, an infusion given twice a year, for relapsing-remitting MS in patients 10 and older. In a trial of 187 children and teens, it controlled relapses at least as well as fingolimod, with fewer new lesions.

stories.title: MS Education Summit in Aurora, Colorado, Saturday
stories.summary: The Rocky Mountain MS Center is hosting a morning of talks on MS care and treatment, from 9 AM to 12:15 PM. The listing says in person; the title mentions an online option, but no access details are given.

stories.title: Remibrutinib pill cut relapses versus Aubagio in two large trials
stories.summary: Company news: Novartis reports two Phase 3 trials in about 2,000 people with relapsing MS. The pill remibrutinib cut yearly relapses by 31% to 35% compared with Aubagio. Its effect on disability was not firmly proven.
stories.why: It is not approved yet; the company plans to seek approval.

stories.title: Active people with MS reported better quality of life
stories.summary: In a survey of 1,083 adults with MS, high physical activity went with better mobility, less fatigue and less walking disability. It is a link, not proof, and the data were self-reported.

stories.title: First dose given in trial of myelin-repair pill PRO-1562
stories.summary: Company news: Progentos has started an early safety trial in healthy adults in Australia. Benefits so far come only from animal studies. A later phase will test people with relapsing MS.
stories.why: No approved drug can rebuild lost myelin yet, so early trials like this are watched closely.

stories.title: Word-finding trouble in MS may be more than slow thinking
stories.summary: In a small study of 38 people with relapsing MS and 23 without, people with MS were slower and made slightly more errors on naming tasks. The errors were not fully explained by slower thinking speed.

stories.title: A 10-day ocean sailing trip looked safe in a small MS study
stories.summary: In a small study of 15 adults with mild to moderate MS and no comparison group, strength, walking, balance and thinking did not change after a 10-day sailing expedition. Most had mild or moderate seasickness, and there were no serious problems.
stories.why: It suggests sailing may be a workable way to stay active, but larger studies are needed.

stories.title: UK study puts a number on the healthcare cost of MS
stories.summary: Researchers at Bangor University looked at nearly 6,000 people with MS. Average healthcare costs were about £2,800 over three months, and almost £9,400 for people with significant disability and fast-changing disease.
stories.why: The study also found MS ranked in the lowest 10% of quality-of-life scores among common long-term conditions.

stories.title: Antioxidant add-on NAC linked to better outcomes in an early MS study
stories.summary: Jefferson University researchers added N-acetylcysteine (NAC), an antioxidant supplement, to people's usual MS treatment and report better outcomes in most. Brain scans also showed better connection between brain regions. The team says larger studies are needed.

stories.title: Workplace exposure to petroleum-based lubricants linked to higher MS odds
stories.summary: A Swedish study of about 2,900 people with MS and 6,100 without found those who reported job exposure to oils and lubricants had 38% higher odds of MS. It is a link, not proof, and exposure was self-reported.
stories.why: It adds to research on workplace and environmental factors, but it does not show that lubricants cause MS.

stories.title: Low-fat diet and fatigue in MS: small trial analysis
stories.summary: In a small four-month trial of 27 adults, fatigue scores improved in both the low-fat diet and usual-diet groups, and the difference between them could be chance. Changes in fat-related blood markers tracked with less fatigue.
stories.why: Diet is not a proven fatigue treatment yet; larger studies are needed.

stories.title: Why some people with MS turn down thinking tests
stories.summary: In one Canadian clinic, about 15% of 334 adults with MS declined free cognitive testing. Those with progressive MS or anxiety-related conditions were more likely to decline, as were those who did not report memory worries.
stories.why: Skipped testing can leave thinking changes unnoticed.

stories.title: Dutch regulator probes Biogen over Tysabri safety test access
stories.summary: The Netherlands' competition authority is examining whether Biogen unfairly kept a Tysabri safety-screening test from patients taking rival drugs, such as a biosimilar. This is an investigation, not a finding.

stories.title: Remote rehab did not beat home exercise for MS in a review
stories.summary: A review pooled five trials and found video-guided remote rehabilitation did no better than home exercise for physical function, balance or quality of life. The authors say the evidence is thin and more good trials are needed.
stories.why: Home exercise may work about as well as remote rehab programs.

stories.title: Column: an MS story doesn't need a neat ending
stories.summary: A columnist who lives with MS writes that hard experiences don't have to be turned into life lessons. This is a personal opinion piece, not research.

stories.title: Starting Ocrevus early linked to less disability over 10 years
stories.summary: A company-funded 10-year follow-up of two large trials in relapsing MS found people who started Ocrevus right away had a 24% lower risk of confirmed disability progression than those who started two years later. No new safety concerns appeared.
stories.why: Suggests timing of treatment may matter, but this is a follow-up analysis, not a new trial.

stories.title: MRI technique may show signs of myelin repair in MS
stories.summary: A study from China of 145 people with MS found that rises in an MRI myelin measure inside lesions tracked with better disability scores over about a year. It was observational, a link, not proof, and the scan is not yet validated.

stories.title: Music-based program for thinking and mood tested in small MS trial
stories.summary: In a small trial of 29 people with MS, a music program was found acceptable, with some hints of lower anxiety and depression. Most thinking-test differences were not statistically significant.
stories.why: The authors say larger trials are needed before drawing conclusions.

stories.title: Column: why we need more research on menopause and MS
stories.summary: A reader-written opinion column by a woman with MS argues that little research looks at how menopause affects MS symptoms and treatment. She calls for neurologists and gynecologists to talk more.

stories.title: Family-focused education program improved well-being in small Iranian trial
stories.summary: In a randomized trial of 70 people with MS and their caregivers in Iran, pairs who took a family-centered program had bigger gains in healthy habits and well-being than pairs given a booklet. The gains were still seen 2 months later.
stories.why: It suggests that involving family in MS self-care may help, though this was a small study from one center.

stories.title: MS specialists discuss gaps in care and what is next
stories.summary: At a clinical forum, MS specialists said strong drugs control relapses but may not stop disability from building up. They saw CAR-T cell therapy as promising but noted open safety questions. This is expert opinion, not a new study.
stories.why: Symptoms like bladder trouble, vertigo and vision problems were named as priorities that patients care about.

stories.title: Brain shrinkage in MS appears to start in busy hub regions
stories.summary: An MRI study of 2,187 people with MS found tissue loss begins in highly connected brain areas, then spreads along linked pathways. Network measures from standard MRI also helped predict later shrinkage.
stories.why: It may one day help doctors spot who is at risk of more brain volume loss.

stories.title: A decade of myelin-repair trials: repair seems possible, benefit not yet shown
stories.summary: A Cambridge researcher says trials suggest myelin can be repaired in people, but clear gains in daily function have not been shown yet. He calls for more sensitive measures, earlier enrollment and longer follow-up.

stories.title: Expert: thinking changes in MS may be more than slow processing speed
stories.summary: In a podcast, a Mount Sinai neuropsychologist said earlier diagnosis and better drugs may have changed how thinking problems look in MS. Word-finding and memory trouble are often reported even when speed tests fall in the normal range.
stories.why: It supports taking brain fog and word-finding trouble seriously and mentioning them to your care team.

stories.title: Cholesterol and inflammation markers tied to disability in progressive MS
stories.summary: In a study of 106 people with progressive MS, those who could no longer walk had lower HDL ("good") cholesterol and higher inflammation markers than those who could still walk. It is a link, not proof of cause.
stories.why: It may help researchers find blood markers of worsening disability.

stories.title: FDA clears testing of privosegtor for acute MS relapses
stories.summary: Company news: Oculis says the FDA cleared it to begin studying the experimental drug privosegtor for sudden MS relapses. It is not approved, and earlier results came from optic neuritis, not MS relapse trials.

stories.title: Probiotic supplement may ease MS fatigue in small Iranian trial
stories.summary: In a small trial of 54 adults with relapsing MS, fatigue rose less over 30 days in people taking a probiotic and prebiotic mix than in those taking placebo.
stories.why: Fatigue is a common MS symptom, but this was small and short, so larger studies are needed.

stories.title: Experimental pill GV300 helped repair myelin in mice
stories.summary: In mice, the ROCK2-blocking drug GV300 lowered inflammation and nerve-covering damage and supported repair. This is company news from lab work, with no human results yet.

stories.title: Health insurance changes in 2027 may affect people with MS
stories.summary: MSAA outlines changes to Medicaid and Medicare, including a $2,400 Medicare drug cap and new Medicaid renewal rules, many starting January 1, 2027.
stories.why: Open enrollment is a good time to review your coverage.

stories.title: Most people on cladribine kept their thinking skills over 4 years
stories.summary: In a follow-up of 280 people with highly active relapsing MS, about 7 in 10 had no or minimal decline on a processing-speed test. There was no comparison group, and over a third still had new or growing MRI lesions.
stories.why: Shows how thinking skills held up for one MS pill, but this follow-up cannot prove the drug was the cause.

stories.title: FDA clears limited access to experimental cell therapy NG01 for progressive MS
stories.summary: Company news: the FDA cleared an expanded access program for NG01, an unapproved therapy made from a patient's own cells. It is for some people with progressive MS who cannot join trials, starting at the University of Miami.
stories.why: It is not approved and its evidence comes from one small earlier trial, so talk with your neurologist.

stories.title: Brooklyn woman marks 40 years with MS, planning her energy each day
stories.summary: A 79-year-old woman with secondary progressive MS describes managing fatigue, walking and vision trouble. Her neurologist says older adults need care that covers mobility, thinking and rehab, not only medicine.

stories.title: Men with MS ranked sexual health as their top research priority
stories.summary: In an Australian survey of 775 men with MS, sexual function ranked first among 14 men's health topics. Sexual difficulties affect an estimated 50 to 90 percent of men with MS.
stories.why: It is common, and men can raise it with their care team.

stories.title: Review: MS fatigue may partly come from extra effort to move
stories.summary: Researchers reviewing existing evidence suggest that some MS fatigue comes from the motor system working harder and recovering less fully after activity. It is a review that proposes ideas to test, not a new trial.

stories.title: Experimental molecule furapyrrodole aided brain repair in mice
stories.summary: In lab cells and mice with an MS-like condition, the molecule helped cells mature into myelin-making cells and improved movement. This is early lab work, not tested in people.

stories.title: Six small grants fund studies of shared drivers of MS, lupus and diabetes
stories.summary: The National MS Society and two other groups will give six researchers up to $150,000 each for one-year pilot studies. The studies look at biology that may be shared by MS, type 1 diabetes and lupus.
stories.why: Findings in one autoimmune disease may help point to new ideas for MS.

stories.title: Australians with MS asked to share aged care experiences by Dec. 14
stories.summary: MS Australia has opened a 15 to 20 minute online survey about aged care. It will shape the group's submission to a government review of aged care reforms.

stories.title: Column: resting and acupuncture helped one woman reach the dance floor
stories.summary: A doctor with MS writes about severe vertigo that nearly kept her from a night out. She used acupuncture and a deliberate rest and nap to make it. This is one personal opinion piece, not research.

stories.title: Brain volume dipped after childbirth in women with MS, then mostly recovered
stories.summary: In 247 women with MS, total brain volume fell by about 0.9% in the first three months after childbirth and generally returned toward earlier levels within one to two years. Lesion volume did not change. The study shows a link, not proof of cause.
stories.why: The researchers say the dip appears to be a normal part of pregnancy rather than a sign of MS getting worse.

stories.title: MS specialist: relapses are better controlled, progression still a gap
stories.summary: In an interview, Cleveland Clinic neurologist Robert Bermel said modern drugs control inflammation and relapses well, but progressive MS is still hard to treat and track. He said oral BTK inhibitors are a promising near-term option, based on early trial results.
stories.why: It shows where MS care is improving and where research is still needed.

stories.title: FDA authorizes first blood test of neurofilament light chain for MS
stories.summary: The FDA granted marketing authorization to Siemens Healthineers for a blood test that measures neurofilament light chain, a sign of nerve injury. It is meant to help doctors check ongoing disease activity in adults 18 to 55 with relapsing-remitting MS. This is company news.
stories.why: It is meant to be used alongside exams and MRI, not instead of them.

stories.title: Chronic low-grade inflammation linked to higher MS risk in large study
stories.summary: In about 377,000 UK adults followed for a median of nearly 14 years, higher blood inflammation scores went with a 38% higher chance of later being diagnosed with MS. This is a link, not proof that inflammation causes MS.

stories.title: MS Trust podcast reviews highlights from the 2026 ECTRIMS research meeting
stories.summary: A podcast episode covers earlier diagnosis, preventing MS, new treatments, women's health, AI and wearables, and living well with MS.
stories.why: A plain-language way to catch up on this year's big research meeting.

stories.title: Free online talk Wednesday on research from the 2026 ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS meeting
stories.summary: Overcoming MS hosts a panel on MSToronto2026 research, 7:00 to 8:15 PM GMT on November 25. It is online and aimed at both newly diagnosed people and those who have lived with MS for years.

stories.title: FDA reviewing one-infusion start for Briumvi
stories.summary: Company news: TG Therapeutics says the FDA accepted its request to let Briumvi treatment begin with one infusion instead of two. A decision is due by July 10, 2027, and the current two-infusion start stays in place until then.
stories.why: If approved, starting this MS drug could take one clinic visit fewer.

stories.title: Older adults on Ocrevus had more infection hospital stays
stories.summary: In a records review of 1,600 people with MS aged 55 and older, those on Ocrevus were hospitalized for infections more than twice as often as those not on it. It was an observational study, so it shows a link, not proof.

stories.title: Free MS medications symposium in Melbourne today
stories.summary: MS Australia and the Florey Institute mark 30 years of MS drug treatments with talks on how care has changed and what is coming next. It is in person only, free, and registration is required.

stories.title: Mouse study: genes may shape how the body controls an EBV-like virus
stories.summary: In mice infected with a virus related to Epstein-Barr, strains that controlled it poorly built up virus-specific immune cells in the brain before any autoimmune disease appeared. This is mouse work, not human data.
stories.why: It may help explain why most people carry Epstein-Barr virus but only some develop MS.

stories.title: Column: the hardest part of MS migraines is the waiting in between
stories.summary: A columnist with MS describes living with migraines that come and go, and the worry about when the next one will arrive. This is one person's account, not research.

stories.title: Low vitamin D common in Saudi MS group; link to fatigue confidence unclear
stories.summary: In 246 adults with MS in one Saudi region, about 3 in 4 with a recorded value had vitamin D below 30 ng/mL. Vitamin D showed only a weak, non-linear link to fatigue self-efficacy (confidence in managing fatigue), and not in simpler models. This is a link, not proof.
stories.why: The authors say vitamin D is not the main factor; work interference and body weight mattered more.

stories.title: Smaller hippocampus linked to thinking problems in a small MS study
stories.summary: In a small MRI study of 20 people with MS and 23 without, MS was tied to smaller hippocampal areas and higher brain "entropy" (a measure of signal irregularity). Both tracked with lower thinking-test scores. It is a link at one point in time, not proof of cause.
